summary: Iteration 120 - regression tests for the rejected/pending_approval progress calculation, structured error contract on update of rejected records, and UI treatment of rejected records. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_rejected_progress_iter120.py with 6 tests, all 6 PASS. Directly exercised CompletionService (facility-level) with seeded env records for pending_approval / approved / rejected / mixed, and confirmed progress.completed counts pending_approval + approved but EXCLUDES rejected. Also verified ESGRecordsService.update_record raises HTTPException 400 with structured detail (error, message, rejection_reason, rejected_at, suggestion) for rejected records and that the live HTTP PUT /api/esg-records/records/environment/{id} returns the same JSON-serializable structured body. Frontend: logged in as admin (goyalsomil2001@gmail.com / TestUser123!), opened /environment, found the existing rejected 'Climate Change / Climate Change Adaptation Plan & Implementation' row. UI shows a 'Rejected' label and the rejection reason ('test') plus only a History icon - NO Edit button, exactly as required. No 'Objects are not valid as a React child' error was rendered.

minor.issue: Latent JSON-serialization bug: HTTPException detail on rejected edit includes current.get('rejected_at') and current.get('submitted_at') verbatim. In production data these are ISO strings, but any code path storing them as raw datetime objects (e.g. task_engine.py L828 sets rejected_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)) will cause FastAPI's JSONResponse to raise 'Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable' and the API returns 500 instead of the intended 400 structured error. Recommend coercing to isoformat before putting into detail. Reproduced during test setup when seeding a datetime rejected_at.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In modules/esg_records/service.py update_record, coerce rejected_at (and any other datetime fields) to .isoformat() when building HTTPException(detail=...) to guarantee 400 (not 500) even if legacy records stored them as datetime objects.
critical_code_review_comments: completion_service._calculate_facility_level & _calculate_org_level correctly gate completion on approval_status != 'rejected'. Business logic matches the review spec.

Frontend ESGRecordsDataEntry correctly discriminates on record.approval_status === 'rejected' AND (legacy) record.status === 'rejected' to render the rejection block instead of the edit button. Structured error handler on update failure extracts detail.message (string) and detail.rejection_reason (string) so it will never spread an object into a React child.
Potential JSON-serialization edge case in update_record's HTTPException detail if any datetime field slips through as a raw datetime (see minor issue). Cheap defensive fix recommended.
seed_data_creation: Test file seeds temporary environment_records docs prefixed TEST_ITER120_* with category 'TEST_ITER120_CustomMetric' (avoids DataChecker keyword routing). Cleanup runs on module setup + teardown via _cleanup(). Individual HTTP test deletes its record in a finally block.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The rejected Climate Change / Adaptation Plan record (id 5c851d19-2369-4863-b191-6c29161104b0) currently exists in admin org and is a stable fixture for UI regression on rejected-record rendering. Use it to visually verify Edit button suppression + rejection_reason display in future runs. For CompletionService seed tests, always use a category name that does NOT contain 'water|energy|waste|ghg|emission|scope|social|governance|employee|worker|health|safety|training' otherwise DataChecker routes to a hardcoded category filter and your seed won't match.
rca of the issue: Root cause of the original React child error was that the backend returns HTTPException.detail as a structured dict {error, message, rejection_reason, rejected_at, suggestion}. Frontend was rendering error.response.data.detail directly as a toast message, which React interpreted as an object child. Fix in ESGRecordsDataEntry.js L785-795 branches on typeof detail === 'object' and extracts detail.message (string) plus optional detail.rejection_reason, so React never receives the raw object. Progress calc bug had the same underlying philosophy: rejected records were being treated as 'has_data => completed' in older versions. Fix in completion_service.py L934/1018/1050 adds the guard `is_completed_for_progress = has_data and approval_status != 'rejected'`.
